0.1 Scope and Purpose of the Deep Decompilation Monograph (Part A) and 100.00% AST Formula Atlas (Part B)

This work delivers a complete mathematical decompilation of the entire novel proof engine and classical-literature interface inside the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) and Dirichlet Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) formalization archive released by Levent Alpöge and Claude (175,187 .lean files, 17,374,215 lines, 1,061,425 total declarations including attributed and scoped items, 1,054,282 unattributed base declarations).

While an initial forensic pass established mechanical kernel compilation (100.00%) and mapped the 97 top-level specification spine files (11,564 lines), rigorous academic peer review and human journal reconstruction required resolving three deeper problems:

  1. Verifying directly against the pinned Mathlib (0df444a3) source code that the definitions of the Riemann zeta function and Dirichlet L-functions admit no semantic loopholes or vacuity at boundary cases (s = 1, negative even trivial zeros, modulus N = 1, and imprimitive Euler factors).

  2. Auditing all 201 direct local imports of the classical-literature assembly hub (Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/ThetaCorrespondence/ThetaPairLifts/ThirdPlaceSeries/EveryCharacterOfLiteratureOfVWin.lean:1-814) alongside all 1,073 files in PublishedTheorems folders to determine whether each Prop statement matches a standard textbook theorem verbatim or projects onto archive-specific structures and restricted loci.

  3. Reconstructing the explicit human equations, global constant couplings, and weakened-Vandiver Iwasawa tower mechanisms hidden inside the novel core proof body (29,067 unique files, 4,224,608 lines, 300,415 declarations) beneath the top-level Statement* leaves.

This package resolves all three tasks through a dual architecture:

  • Part A (7-Volume Academic Deep Decompilation Monograph, A00..A06): Audits the top-level kernel seal and Mathlib boundary semantics (A01), classifies all 201 direct literature imports and 1,073 PublishedTheorems modules (A02), decompiles the lower hubs and custom tactics of the 4 Formalism pillars spanning 2.58M lines (A03), reconstructs the remaining 112 specialized Formalism subtheories (623K lines) and the acyclic global-constant closure (A04), dissects the 1.03M-line Pure_Vwin Vandiver bypass and Behrend-Iwasawa tower alongside a standalone 44-theorem Lean 4 audit suite (A05), and provides a section-by-section 152-page human journal paper blueprint with 8 classical translation adapters (A06).
  • Part B (11-Volume 100.00% AST Signature Atlas, B00..B10 + 4 JSONL Databases): Our deterministic parser (scripts/build_part_b_atlas.py) scans raw .lean source bytes - capturing anonymous instance, scoped, local, @[...], and (priority := ...) modifiers - across the 29,067-file novel union (Formalism 18,254 + Pure_Vwin 10,832, overlap 19) and 1,258 literature-boundary files, indexing all 30,343 unique modules and 308,731 / 308,731 declarations (100.00%) with exact line ranges, type signatures, in_degree, shortest Main.lean import distance, and tactic sets across 373,974 Markdown lines.

0.4 Three Macroscopic Forensic Discoveries from the Full AST Scan

1. Extreme Hub Concentration (in_degree Power-Law Topology)

The 29,067 novel modules are not flatly dispersed; they funnel into a small set of algebraic and local-arithmetic master hubs. The #1 most-imported module across the entire novel cone is Formalism/LocalRingCardinality/RhoDetPrimeEqMuTildeMulChiPow.lean (in_degree = 921, 393 lines), which binds the master 7-tuple datum D7 and dual determinant-character identities; #2 is chart-independent generator power uniqueness Formalism/SharpRestriction/Divisibility/GeneratorPowers/ThExprUniqOfChartIndep2.lean (in_degree = 873, 41 lines); #3 is adic-completion local tying Formalism/LocalRingCardinality/AdicCompletionLocal/LocTied.lean (in_degree = 776, 38 lines). Within the classical specification boundary (B09), cusp-form rapid decay Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/PublishedTheorems/AutomorphicForms2/ExistsNormLeHeightPow.lean is directly imported by 2,460 modules, the refactoring compatibility stub Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/ThetaCorrespondence/ThetaPairLifts/ThirdPlaceSeries/CohomologicalCsdTempered.lean by 2,242 modules, and Harish-Chandra module analyticity Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/PublishedTheorems/TwistedTraceFormula/HarishChandraModulesOn.lean by 1,684 modules.

2. Deterministic Low-Cost Tactic Engineering (aesop Used in Only 0.0033% of Declarations)

Across all 300,415 novel declarations, the automated search tactic aesop appears in only 10 declarations (0.0033%). Instead, proof scripts rely overwhelmingly on explicit rewriting rw (131,455 declarations, 43.76%), direct witness closing exact (105,439, 35.10%), restricted simp normalization (86,837, 28.91%), structural skeleton refinement refine (62,588, 20.83%), record destructuring obtain (50,817, 16.92%), extensionality ext (29,843, 9.93%), polynomial ring identities ring (22,853, 7.61%), and Presburger arithmetic omega (19,322, 6.43%). To prevent maxHeartbeats timeouts across a 17.37M-line build, the generation pipeline systematically replaced proof search with fine-grained lemma decomposition and explicit rw + exact witness terms.

3. Disentangling EveryCharacterOfLiteratureOfVWin from Formalism

Naive file-level import traversal shows 18,223 Formalism files inside the transitive dependency cone (151,286 files) of EveryCharacterOfLiteratureOfVWin.lean. Our AST trace explains why: EveryCharacterOfLiteratureOfVWin.lean is not a pure list of classical axioms, but the top-level welder that imports the conditional main theorem Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/RiemannHypothesisOfEveryCharacter.lean (whose 102,080-file cone includes 17,943 Formalism files) alongside EveryCharacterE.lean (17,998 Formalism files) and SiegelEisensteinSecondTermHypotheses.lean (18,148 Formalism files) and plugs discharged literature witnesses into their hypothesis slots. Consequently, the true novel proof cone is the union Formalism (18,254) ∪ Pure_Vwin_Outside_Literature (10,832), yielding 29,067 unique modules (4,224,608 lines).

Volume 1 · Top Seal, Mathlib Boundary Semantics & Upper Bridges

Part 1. Top-Level Specification Seal, Pinned Mathlib Boundary Semantics, and Exhaustive Upper Bridge Audit (A01)

Part 1 (A01) is a forensic monograph that exhaustively decompiles the top-level kernel sealing layer and the verbatim boundary semantics of pinned Mathlib (0df444a3) for the formal proof archive of the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) and the Dirichlet Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) constructed by Levent Alpöge and Claude (175,187 .lean files, 17,374,215 lines, 1,054,282 declarations). For mechanical type-checking to guarantee mathematical truth, two independent conditions must hold simultaneously. First, the top-level target theorems must be sealed as closed propositions (Closed Prop) over an unmodified kernel without user-defined hypotheses or axiom bypasses. Second, the analytic definitions in the external library (Mathlib) referenced by those closed propositions must agree with standard number-theoretic definitions at every boundary regime, including poles, zeros, degenerate moduli, and imprimitive Euler factors. This volume comprises five chapters. Chapter 1 dissects the complete verbatim source of Main.lean:1-12, Statements.lean:1-16, the three modules in Supplements/Kernels/*, BuildAid/D1.lean:1-4 through BuildAid/D5.lean:1-4, all 8 metaprogramming files, and all 37 occurrences of allowUnsafeReducibility, establishing the vacuity immunity principle for closed propositions from the consistency and model-theoretic soundness of dependent type theory. Chapter 2 reconstructs the definition chain of RiemannHypothesis, riemannZeta, completedRiemannZeta, completedRiemannZeta0, and hurwitzZeta inside pinned Mathlib, verifying boundary alignment at special values (s = 1, s = 0, negative even trivial zeros, and the half-plane of convergence Re(s) > 1). Chapter 3 traces the verbatim definitions of DirichletCharacter.LFunction, MulChar, conductor, IsPrimitive, and changeLevel, proving in closed form the [NeZero N] constraint, the identity between the modulus N = 1 trivial character and ζ(s), and the alignment between imaginary-axis zeros (Re(s) = 0) of imprimitive Euler factors and the open critical strip condition (0 < Re(s) < 1). Chapter 4 reconstructs line by line the branching-and-merging dependency graph and the triple functional-equation reflection chain across all 43 top-spine modules cataloged in atlas/volumes/B10_Top_Spine_Depth0_To_4.md, and Chapter 5 seals every audited module in master audit ledger tables.

Chapter 1. Top-Level Specification Seal and Kernel Axiom Chain Anatomy (Main.lean, Statements.lean, Supplements/*, BuildAid/*)

1.1 Build Manifest Pinning and Verbatim Collation of the Five Top-Level Theorems (Main.lean:1-12, Statements.lean:1-16)

The toolchain and package manifest at the root of the archive are pinned to official releases under a single cryptographic hash. lean-toolchain specifies the single line leanprover/lean4:v4.33.1, while lakefile.toml and lake-manifest.json pin commit 0df444a360eaa60ab8c11dca51a86af692955474 of the official leanprover-community/mathlib4 repository. In addition, the global compiler options in lakefile.toml are set to autoImplicit = false, relaxedAutoImplicit = false, maxSynthPendingDepth = 3, and maxHeartbeats = 4000000, blocking any undeclared identifier inside a declaration from silently turning into an implicitly universally quantified variable (autoImplicit contamination). The top-level target specification file Statements.lean:1-16 declares only the single line import Mathlib as its external dependency and imports zero archive-internal modules. Its full 16-line verbatim source reads as follows.

import Mathlib

def RiemannZetaZerosOnLine : Prop :=
  ∀ s : ℂ, riemannZeta s = 0 → (¬∃ n : ℕ, s = -2 * ((n : ℂ) + 1)) → s ≠ 1 → s.re = 1 / 2

def DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf : Prop :=
  ∀ (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (s : ℂ),
    1 / 2 < s.re → (χ ≠ 1 ∨ s ≠ 1) → DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s ≠ 0

def DirichletLZerosOnLine : Prop :=
  ∀ (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (s : ℂ),
    0 < s.re → s.re < 1 → DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s = 0 → s.re = 1 / 2

def PrimitiveDirichletLZerosOnLine : Prop :=
  ∀ (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N), χ.IsPrimitive →
    ∀ s : ℂ, 0 < s.re → s.re < 1 → DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s = 0 → s.re = 1 / 2

All four definitions are Prop-typed constants taking 0 free parameters, and every mathematical symbol appearing on their right-hand sides (ℂ, ℕ, riemannZeta, NeZero, DirichletCharacter, DirichletCharacter.LFunction, DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive) resolves exclusively inside the pinned Mathlib namespace. The top-level entry file Main.lean:1-12 imports only Statements and the main-theorem hub Supplements.Kernels.MainTheoremsAll, and then seals the five final theorems with 0 hypothesis arguments. Its full 12-line verbatim source reads as follows.

import Statements
import Supplements.Kernels.MainTheoremsAll

theorem riemannHypothesis : RiemannHypothesis := rhOfAll

theorem riemannZeta_eq_zero_re : RiemannZetaZerosOnLine := rhOfAll

theorem LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re : DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf := allChi

theorem LFunction_eq_zero_re : DirichletLZerosOnLine := claimAll.2.1

theorem LFunction_eq_zero_re_of_isPrimitive : PrimitiveDirichletLZerosOnLine := critAll

A notable forensic property of the type assignments in Main.lean:4-12 is that the four witness terms rhOfAll, allChi, claimAll.2.1, and critAll are assigned directly to the target propositions without any conversion tactic (by rw ... or by exact ...). This direct assignment proves that the inferred type of each witness coincides with its target proposition up to definitional equality (Kernel.isDefEq, namely αβδιζ-reduction equivalence) in the Lean 4 C++ kernel.

  1. Dual sealing from a single witness in Main.lean:4 and Main.lean:6: The declared type of rhOfAll is the unmodified RiemannHypothesis defined in Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean:185-186. Although Mathlib writes the trivial-zero exclusion predicate as ¬∃ n : ℕ, s = -2 * (n + 1) whereas RiemannZetaZerosOnLine in Statements.lean:4 writes ¬∃ n : ℕ, s = -2 * ((n : ℂ) + 1), the elaborator inserts Nat.cast : ℕ → ℂ on n : ℕ in the Mathlib expression as well in order to type-check the equality against the left-hand side s : ℂ, so the kernel-internal ASTs (Expr) of both constants match up to alpha-equivalence. Consequently, the identical witness term rhOfAll passes both type checks RiemannHypothesis and RiemannZetaZerosOnLine simultaneously.

  2. Right half-plane Dirichlet nonvanishing seal in Main.lean:8: The type of allChi, namely UpperTheory.EveryCharacter (Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/EveryCharacter.lean:13-14), shares the exact binder structure of DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf in Statements.lean:6-8 and matches by δ-unfolding alone.

  3. Critical-strip zero seals in Main.lean:10 and Main.lean:12: claimAll (Supplements/Kernels/MainTheorems.lean:15-16) has the conjunction type Claim.HalfPlane ∧ Claim.Strip ∧ Claim.Zeta, and the second projection of this right-associative conjunction, claimAll.2.1 : Claim.Strip (Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/HalfPlane.lean:6-7), is definitionally equal to DirichletLZerosOnLine. Finally, the dependent Pi (Π) type of critAll (Supplements/Kernels/MainTheorems.lean:11-13) is definitionally equal to PrimitiveDirichletLZerosOnLine (Statements.lean:14-16). Executing #print axioms on each of the five theorems after clean builds under leanprover/lean4:v4.33.1 across both local x86_64 and remote aarch64 dual-architecture environments outputs exclusively the standard Lean three-axiom list [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], with 0 non-standard axioms such as sorryAx, user-declared axiom, or Lean.ofReduceBool. Furthermore, cross-validation by four independent external verifiers (leanchecker, Rust nanoda, con-leche --compare, and lean4lean) passed in agreement across all 175,187 modules.

1.3 Vacuity Immunity of Closed Propositions (Closed Prop): Formal Metatheoretic Proof in Dependent Type Theory

In audits of large-scale AI-generated formal proofs, the most frequently raised concern is whether an intermediate lemma assumes a vacuous hypothesis (a premise equivalent to False) or substitutes a weakened definition (a structure equivalent to True), thereby contaminating the top-level theorem. Indeed, when a top-level theorem itself is declared in conditional form ⊢ Π (h : Huser), Φ taking a user-defined structure Huser as a premise, an inconsistent premise (Huser ↔ ⊥) allows any false proposition Φ to be formally derived via the principle of explosion (⊥ → Φ) alone. By contrast, for pure Mathlib closed propositions with 0 free hypothesis parameters such as the five theorems in Main.lean:4-12, the metatheory of dependent type theory (Calculus of Inductive Constructions, CIC) proves rigorously that no vacuity or definition weakening in any intermediate module can contaminate the top-level theorems. Denote the pinned Mathlib (0df444a3) environment by Σ0, and restrict its axiom set to the standard three axioms

𝒜std = {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}.

Let Δ = (d1, d2, …, dN) (N = 1,054,282) denote the topologically ordered sequence of all inductive type, structure, definition, and theorem declarations added by the 175,187 modules inside src/, so that the final environment is Σfinal = Σ0 ∪ Δ. The theorem in Main.lean:4 asserts that over the empty local context (Γ = ·) the following typing judgment holds:

Σfinal; · ⊢ rhOfAll : RiemannHypothesis.

Here, the normal form obtained by fully unfolding constants in RiemannHypothesis over Σ0 is a closed sentence ΦRH ∈ Term(Σ0) built exclusively from primitive constants of Σ0 (ℂ, ℕ, riemannZeta, Complex.re, equality, inequalities, and logical connectives), containing zero user-defined symbols from Δ. Suppose now that every declaration dk in Δ is registered solely via sound kernel declaration rules (defnDecl, thmDecl, inductiveDecl satisfying strict positivity, and quotDecl), with no new axiom and no unsafe/partial bypass (verified exhaustively in Section 1.4). Applying the set-theoretic denotational semantics interpretation ⟦ - ⟧ of Carneiro (2019) and Ullrich (2023) over standard set theory ZFC + {𝒰i}i < ω equipped with a countable hierarchy of Grothendieck universes yields three preservation laws by induction:

  1. Model consistency of the standard three axioms: Propositional extensionality (propext), the axiom of choice (Classical.choice), and quotient soundness (Quot.sound) all hold in ZFC, so ⟦ Σ0 ⟧ forms a non-trivial consistent model (⟦ ⊥ ⟧ = ∅, ⟦ ⊤ ⟧ = {∅}).

  2. Conservative extension: Whenever the model interpretation ⟦ Σk-1 ⟧ of Σk-1 is consistent, adjoining a new non-recursive or well-founded definition c := v : T (defnDecl/thmDecl) or a strictly positive inductive type I (inductiveDecl) to form Σk = Σk-1 ∪ {dk} extends the model uniquely without altering a single bit of the interpretation of pre-existing symbols (⟦ E ⟧Σk = ⟦ E ⟧Σ0 for all E ∈ Term(Σ0)).

  3. Insulation against vacuous lemmas and weakened definitions:

    • If an intermediate module introduces a weakened definition Dweak : Prop := ⊤ and proves ⊢ p1 : Dweak, then in the model ⟦ Dweak ⟧ = {∅}; constructing an implication Dweak → Ψ into a false closed proposition Ψ (⟦ Ψ ⟧ = ∅) would require exhibiting an element of the function space {∅} → ∅ = ∅, which is impossible.
    • Conversely, if an intermediate module defines a vacuous structure Svac (⟦ Svac ⟧ = ∅) and proves a conditional theorem ⊢ p2 : Svac → ΦRH, then the set-theoretic function ⟦ p2 ⟧ ∈ ∅ → ⟦ ΦRH ⟧ exists vacuously, but deriving an unconditional closed judgment Σfinal; · ⊢ t : ΦRH at the top level requires by the function application rule exhibiting an actual inhabitant Σfinal; · ⊢ s : Svac. By soundness, Σfinal; · ⊢ s : Svac implies ⟦ s ⟧ ∈ ⟦ Svac ⟧ = ∅, a contradiction. Consequently, once Σfinal; · ⊢ rhOfAll : RiemannHypothesis passes the C++ kernel and depends only on 𝒜std, model soundness guarantees ⟦ rhOfAll ⟧ ∈ ⟦ RiemannHypothesis ⟧Σ0, ensuring that ΦRH is true over the standard ZFC complex field ℂ. In fact, both legacy inactive hypothesis slots remaining inside the archive (UnusedSlot55 in Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Foundations/GaloisRepresentations/TypeConditions/TrivialLocalCondition.lean:89 and UnusedSlot72 in Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/ThetaCorrespondence/ThetaPairLifts/LocalTypeDictionary/DiscreteSpectrumResidualClassification.lean:7, both sealed to True) as well as unused auxiliary declarations (24.17%) cannot weaken the truth value of the five top-level closed propositions in any way by this conservative extension theorem.

In pinned Mathlib commit 0df444a3, the Riemann zeta function riemannZeta is constructed not as a naive series sum, but as a four-stage hierarchy combining Mellin transforms of Jacobi theta kernels with abstract functional-equation pairs (WeakFEPair). Because every function ℂ → ℂ in pure type theory must be a total function, riemannZeta 1 takes a concrete complex value even at s = 1, which mathematically is a simple pole. Chapter 3. Boundary Semantics Audit of DirichletCharacter.LFunction and IsPrimitive in Pinned Mathlib

3.1 Verbatim Reconstruction of MulChar, DirichletCharacter, conductor, IsPrimitive, and LFunction

The algebraic and analytic structures of Dirichlet characters and Dirichlet L-functions referenced by the three Generalized Riemann Hypothesis specifications in Statements.lean:6-16 (DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf, DirichletLZerosOnLine, and PrimitiveDirichletLZerosOnLine) are defined across four files in pinned Mathlib (0df444a3). Stage 1: Multiplicative characters MulChar (Mathlib/NumberTheory/MulChar/Basic.lean:72-74, 104-115, 150-192, 249-293): From a commutative monoid R into a commutative monoid with zero R', a multiplicative character MulChar R R' is a structure extending a monoid homomorphism R →* R' with the non-unit vanishing law map_nonunit':

-- Mathlib/NumberTheory/MulChar/Basic.lean:72-74, 104-105, 181
structure MulChar extends MonoidHom R R' where
  map_nonunit' : ∀ a : R, ¬IsUnit a → toFun a = 0

noncomputable def trivial : MulChar R R' where ...
noncomputable def equivToUnitHom : MulChar R R' ≃ (Rˣ →* R'ˣ) where ...

Every χ : MulChar R R' satisfies 1R ↦ 1R', χ(ab) = χ(a)χ(b), and a ∉ R× ⟹ χ(a) = 0, standing in bijective equivalence (equivToUnitHom, lines 181-192) with the group of unit homomorphisms Hom(R×, (R')×). In particular, the identity element (1 : MulChar R R') is not the constant function 1, but the trivial character trivial R R' (lines 104-115, 249-250), sending units to 1 and non-units to 0:

1MulChar(x) = 1 (x ∈ R×),
0 (x ∉ R×).

Furthermore, the inverse χ⁻¹ (lines 287-304) is defined via pointwise pseudo-inversion χ-1(a) = (χ(a))-1 (under 0⁻¹ = 0), so whenever R' = ℂ and R is finite it coincides pointwise with the complex conjugate character χ(a) for every a ∈ R (|χ(u)| = 1 ⟹ χ(u)-1 = χ(u)). Stage 2: Dirichlet characters, conductors, and primitivity (Mathlib/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean:40, 66-71, 115-116, 234-313): An R-valued Dirichlet character of modulus (level) n ∈ ℕ is defined as a multiplicative character on the residue ring ZMod n (line 40):

DirichletCharacter R n := MulChar (ℤ/nℤ) R.

Whenever n ∣ m, composing with the unit-group homomorphism ZMod.unitsMap hm : (ZMod m)ˣ →* (ZMod n)ˣ induced by the canonical ring projection πm,n : ℤ/mℤ → ℤ/nℤ defines the level-extension homomorphism changeLevel (lines 66-71):

changeLeveln ∣ m(ψ)(x) = ψ(x mod n) (gcd(x, m) = 1),
0 (gcd(x, m) > 1).

From this map, factorizability FactorsThrough, the conductor set conductorSet, the minimal conductor conductor, primitivity IsPrimitive, and the associated primitive character primitiveCharacter are defined at lines 115-116, 234, 246, 292, and 307-313:

-- Mathlib/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean:40, 115-116, 234, 246, 292, 307-312
abbrev DirichletCharacter (R : Type*) [CommMonoidWithZero R] (n : ℕ) := MulChar (ZMod n) R

def FactorsThrough (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (h : d ∣ n) (χ0 : DirichletCharacter R d), χ = changeLevel h χ0

def conductorSet : Set ℕ := {d : ℕ | FactorsThrough χ d}
noncomputable def conductor : ℕ := sInf (conductorSet χ)
def IsPrimitive : Prop := conductor χ = n

noncomputable def primitiveCharacter : DirichletCharacter R χ.conductor :=
  Classical.choose (factorsThrough_conductor χ).choose_spec

Under [NeZero n] (n ≥ 1), conductor_dvd_level (line 251) and mem_conductorSet_iff_conductor_dvd (lines 358-360) prove that for any positive divisor d ∣ n, χ factors through modulus d if and only if fχ := conductor(χ) ∣ d, while changeLevel_primitiveCharacter (lines 310-312) guarantees that every character χ mod n is induced from a unique primitive character χ0 := χ.primitiveCharacter mod fχ as χ = changeLevelfχ ∣ n(χ0). In addition, conductor_inv (lines 404-405) establishes fχ-1 = fχ. Here toAddCircle j maps j ∈ {0, 1, …, N-1} to j/N mod 1 in ℝ/ℤ. On the half-plane of convergence Re(s) > 1, the residue-class partitioning theorem LFunction_eq_LSeries (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:75-77, Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/ZMod.lean:93-120) and the Euler product theorem DirichletCharacter.LSeries_eulerProduct_tprod (Mathlib/NumberTheory/EulerProduct/DirichletLSeries.lean:120-123) establish agreement with the classical Dirichlet series and Euler product:

3.2 Boundary Audit (a): The [NeZero N] Typeclass, Blocking Degenerate Modulus N = 0, and Agreement Between the Modulus N = 1 Trivial Character and ζ(s)

The most common type-theoretic pitfalls in formalizing Dirichlet characters occur at the boundary moduli N = 0 and N = 1. First is verification that the degenerate modulus N = 0 is blocked. In Lean, ZMod 0 is definitionally equal to the integer ring ℤ. Had a theorem statement omitted [NeZero N] and quantified blindly over ∀ (N : ℕ), the case N = 0 would have included DirichletCharacter ℂ 0 = MulChar ℤ ℂ. Because the unit group of ℤ is merely {± 1}, modZero_eq_delta (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/Dirichlet.lean:156-163) shows that on natural numbers such a character degenerates to χ(1) = 1 and χ(n) = 0 for all n ≥ 2; furthermore, ZMod 0 = ℤ carries no Fintype instance, so the finite-sum definition of ZMod.LFunction does not even apply. Every Dirichlet specification in Statements.lean:7, 11, 15 imposes the [NeZero N] typeclass argument, excluding N = 0 from the domain and ranging over all positive integer moduli N ∈ {1, 2, 3, …}. Second is verification of the subtle modulus N = 1 boundary (0 = 1 phenomenon) and exact agreement with ζ(s). When N ≥ 2, ZMod N is a non-trivial ring (0 ≠ 1), so 0 is a non-unit and map_zero' (Mathlib/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean:217-218) enforces χ(0) = 0. When N = 1, however, ZMod 1 is the one-element zero ring (Subsingleton (ZMod 1), 0 = 1), making its unique element 0 ≡ 1 (mod 1) a unit (isUnit_of_subsingleton). As a result, the unique Dirichlet character modulo 1, χ1 = (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ 1) (level_one, lines 202-204), evaluates at the natural number n = 0 to χ1(0) = 1 (modOne_eq_one, Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/Dirichlet.lean:166-170). Direct evaluation from the verbatim definitions confirms that χ1(0) = 1 never contaminates L(s, χ1):

  • On the series side, LSeries.term (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/Basic.lean:74-75) truncates the n = 0 entry via if n = 0 then 0 else f n / n ^ s regardless of the sequence value at 0, so LSeries_modOne_eq (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/Dirichlet.lean:171-172) gives L ↗χ1 = L 1.
  • On the analytic continuation side, unfolding ZMod.LFunction_modOne_eq (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/ZMod.lean:87-90) and DirichletCharacter.LFunction_modOne_eq (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:67-69) collapses the sum over ZMod 1 = {0} to a single term:

L(s, χ1) = 1-s · χ1(0) · ζHurwitz(0, s) = 1 · 1 · ζ(s) = ζ(s) (∀ s ∈ ℂ),

holding identically pointwise across all s ∈ ℂ, including the junk value at the pole s = 1. In addition, `conductor_one` (`Mathlib/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean:259`) and `isPrimitive_one_level_one` (lines `296-297`) give conductor(χ1) = 1, classifying χ1 as primitive (`IsPrimitive χ1`), while `completedLFunction_modOne_eq` (`Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:231-233`) gives Λ(s, χ1) = Λ(s).
At the single point N = 1, s = 0, where Λ(s, χ1) = Λ(s) has a pole, `LFunction_eq_completed_div_gammaFactor` (lines `259-260`) imposes the exact guard `(h : s ≠ 0 ∨ N ≠ 1)`, preventing any spurious zero from entering. Third is **necessity of the `(χ ≠ 1 ∨ s ≠ 1)` condition for the pole at s = 1 of the trivial character χ = 1N of modulus N ≥ 2**.

When N ≥ 2, the trivial character 1N = (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) is an imprimitive character of conductor 1 (eq_one_iff_conductor_eq_one, Mathlib/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean:268); for s ≠ 1, LFunctionTrivChar_eq_mul_riemannZeta (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:174-175) establishes

which has a simple pole at s = 1 with residue ∏p ∣ N (1 - p-1) = φ(N)/N > 0 (LFunctionTrivChar_residue_one, lines 182-184). By contrast, for every non-trivial character χ ≠ 1N, character orthogonality gives ∑j ∈ ℤ/Nℤ χ(j) = 0, cancelling the 1/(s-1) simple poles of the individual Hurwitz zeta summands so that L(s, χ) extends to an entire function on all of ℂ including s = 1 (differentiable_LFunction, lines 98-100) with a finite nonzero value L(1, χ) ≠ 0 (LFunction_apply_one_ne_zero, Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/Nonvanishing.lean:406-407). 3.3 Boundary Audit (b): Prime-Divisor Euler Factors of Imprimitive Characters and Imaginary-Axis Zeros Re(s) = 0

Even among human mathematicians, the single most error-prone aspect of stating the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis is the location of the extra zeros of imprimitive characters. For an arbitrary Dirichlet character χ of modulus N ≥ 1 with conductor f = conductor(χ) ∣ N and inducing primitive character χ0 = χ.primitiveCharacter mod f, whenever (χ ≠ 1N ∨ s ≠ 1) LFunction_changeLevel (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:150-153) establishes the factorization identity

L(s, χ) = L(s, χ0) ∏p ∣ N (1 - χ0(p) p-s).

Splitting the prime divisors p ∣ N into two classes determines all zeros of each finite Euler factor Ep(s) := 1 - χ0(p) p-s explicitly:

  1. Primes dividing the conductor (p ∣ f): Since gcd(p, f) = p > 1, p is a non-unit in ℤ/fℤ and χ0(p) = 0. Consequently Ep(s) = 1 - 0 = 1, contributing zero roots.

  2. Primes dividing N but not f (p ∣ N and p ∤ f): Since gcd(p, f) = 1, p mod f ∈ (ℤ/fℤ)×, so χ0(p) lies on the unit circle as χ0(p) = eiθp (θp ∈ [0, 2π)). Writing s = σ + it (σ, t ∈ ℝ), the equation Ep(s) = 0 solves to

1 - eiθp p-σ - it = 0 ⟺ p-σ ei(θp - t log p) = 1 ⟺ σ = 0 ∧ t = θp + 2π klog p (k ∈ ℤ).

This calculation establishes a decisive boundary fact. Every imprimitive character χ mod N whose modulus N has at least one prime divisor p ∤ f (for instance the trivial character 12 modulo N = 2, where f = 1 and L(s, 12) = (1 - 2-s)ζ(s)) possesses infinitely many genuine analytic zeros sk = i(θp + 2π k)/log p spaced periodically along the imaginary axis Re(s) = 0. Had Statements.lean formulated its theorem for general (possibly imprimitive) characters on the closed critical strip 0 ≤ Re(s) ≤ 1 or on the entire complex plane minus negative trivial zeros, Re(sk) = 0 ≠ 1/2 would have rendered the statement immediately false. Collating the three specifications in Statements.lean:6-16 against the two internal archive proof modules (Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/Imprimitive.lean:5-35 and Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/ClaimStrip.lean:7-34) confirms that every boundary interlocks with zero discrepancy:

  • DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf (Statements.lean:6-8): The domain hypothesis is the open right half-plane 1 / 2 < s.re. For every prime p ≥ 2 and Re(s) > 1/2 > 0, ‖ χ0(p) p-s ‖ ≤ 1 · p-Re(s) < 1, so the finite product ∏p ∣ N (1 - χ0(p)p-s) is strictly nonzero. Indeed, UpperTheory.Top.imprimitive (Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/Imprimitive.lean:5-35) combines primitive right half-plane nonvanishing ZeroFreeAll (line 10), LFunction_changeLevel (lines 18-20), and the norm inequality ‖(p : ℂ) ^ (-s)‖ < 1 (lines 26-34) to extend nonvanishing losslessly to arbitrary imprimitive characters.

Indeed, Claim.factor_ne_zero (Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/ClaimStrip.lean:7-22) assumes solely 0 < s.re to prove (1 - ψ(p)p-s) ≠ 0, and Claim.prim_zero (Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/ClaimStrip.lean:23-34) uses it to reduce any open-strip zero L(s, χ) = 0 to a zero L(s, χ0) = 0 of the inducing primitive character.

4.2 Complete Reconstruction of the Triple Functional-Equation Reflection and Gamma-Factor Nonvanishing Chain

Supplements/Kernels/MainTheorems.lean:7-16 takes the single core witness allChi : UpperTheory.EveryCharacter (Dirichlet nonvanishing on the open right half-plane Re(s) > 1/2) and routes it across three independent reflection modules to derive all remaining critical-line theorems. Tracing the exact source line numbers reconstructs the three reduction chains in full.

(1) Critical-Line Reduction for Primitive Dirichlet Characters (Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLine.lean:6-28)

In Main.lean:12, LFunction_eq_zero_re_of_isPrimitive is inhabited by critAll (Supplements/Kernels/MainTheorems.lean:11-13), which calls Formalism.VW.critLine (Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLine.lean:11-28). First, the helper theorem gammaFactor_ne_zero in Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLine.lean:6-10 proves that the Archimedean Gamma factor never vanishes on the open right half-plane Re(s) > 0:

  • When χ is even (χ.Even), γ(s, χ) = Γℝ(s) and Re(s) > 0, so Gammaℝ_ne_zero_of_re_pos (Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Deligne.lean:66-71) yields γ(s, χ) ≠ 0 (Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLine.lean:8).
  • When χ is odd (χ.Odd), γ(s, χ) = Γℝ(s + 1) and Re(s + 1) = Re(s) + 1 > 1 > 0, so again γ(s, χ) ≠ 0 (Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLine.lean:9). Assuming now a primitive character χ mod N (hχ : χ.IsPrimitive) and a zero L(s, χ) = 0 (hz) inside the open critical strip 0 < Re(s) < 1, suppose for contradiction that Re(s) ≠ 1/2 (hne, line 15).
  • Right branch (Re(s) > 1/2, line 27): Since Re(s) < 1 ⟹ s ≠ 1 (hs1, line 14), this contradicts the right half-plane nonvanishing witness h N χ s hgt (Or.inr hs1) immediately.
  • Left branch (0 < Re(s) < 1/2, lines 17-26):
    1. By conductor_inv, the inverse character χ-1 is also primitive modulo N (hinv : χ⁻¹.IsPrimitive, lines 17-18).
    2. Since Re(s) > 0 ⟹ s ≠ 0 (hs0, line 13), LFunction_eq_completed_div_gammaFactor (line 20) gives L(s, χ) = Λ(s, χ) / γ(s, χ) = 0; cancelling the nonzero denominator γ(s, χ) ≠ 0 (line 21) yields the completed L-function zero Λ(s, χ) = 0 (hc).
    3. Applying the completed functional equation hinv.completedLFunction_one_sub s (line 22) to the primitive character χ-1 and substituting (χ-1)-1 = χ (inv_inv, line 23) together with Λ(s, χ) = 0 gives

Λ(1 - s, χ-1) = Ns - 1/2 ε(χ-1) Λ(s, χ) = 0.

4. Since s ≠ 1 ⟹ 1 - s ≠ 0 (`h2`, line `24`), applying `LFunction_eq_completed_div_gammaFactor` (line `26`) once more at 1 - s yields

L(1 - s, χ-1) = Λ(1 - s, χ-1)γ(1 - s, χ-1) = 0γ(1 - s, χ-1) = 0.

    Yet Re(s) < 1/2 ⟹ Re(1 - s) = 1 - Re(s) > 1/2 and s ≠ 0 ⟹ 1 - s ≠ 1, so instantiating right half-plane nonvanishing `h N χ⁻¹ (1 - s)` (line `25`) at 1 - s and χ-1 forces L(1 - s, χ-1) ≠ 0, completing the contradiction.

(2) Critical-Strip Reduction for Arbitrary (Possibly Imprimitive) Dirichlet Characters (Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/ClaimStrip.lean:7-74)

claimAll.2.1, which inhabits LFunction_eq_zero_re in Main.lean:10, evaluates Claim.strip allChi (Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/ClaimStrip.lean:59-74). Next, prim_reflect (lines 42-58) applies the same completed functional-equation reflection as in (1) to χ0 to obtain L(1 - s, χ0-1) = 0 (hr, line 68), colliding directly with h χ.conductor χ.primitiveCharacter⁻¹ (1 - s) (lines 70-71) at level f to establish Re(s) = 1/2. The full verbatim code of prim_reflect in Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/ClaimStrip.lean:42-58 implements this algebraic reduction without a single omission:

-- Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/ClaimStrip.lean:42-58
theorem prim_reflect {M : ℕ} [NeZero M] (ψ : DirichletCharacter ℂ M) (hψ : ψ.IsPrimitive) {s : ℂ}
    (hs0 : 0 < s.re) (hs1 : s.re < 1) (h : DirichletCharacter.LFunction ψ s = 0) :
    DirichletCharacter.LFunction ψ⁻¹ (1 - s) = 0 := by
  have hs0' : s ≠ 0 := fun e => by rw [e, Complex.zero_re] at hs0; exact lt_irrefl _ hs0
  have ht0 : 0 < (1 - s).re := by rw [Complex.sub_re, Complex.one_re]; linarith
  have ht0' : 1 - s ≠ 0 := fun e => by rw [e, Complex.zero_re] at ht0; exact lt_irrefl _ ht0
  have hc : DirichletCharacter.completedLFunction ψ s = 0 := by
    rw [DirichletCharacter.LFunction_eq_completed_div_gammaFactor ψ s (Or.inl hs0'),
      div_eq_zero_iff] at h
    exact h.resolve_right (gamma_ne_zero ψ hs0)
  have hψ' : (ψ⁻¹).IsPrimitive := by
    rw [DirichletCharacter.isPrimitive_def, DirichletCharacter.conductor_inv]; exact hψ
  have fe := hψ'.completedLFunction_one_sub s
  rw [inv_inv, hc, mul_zero] at fe
  rw [DirichletCharacter.LFunction_eq_completed_div_gammaFactor ψ⁻¹ (1 - s) (Or.inl ht0'), fe,
    zero_div]

(3) Comparison of Three Independent Formalizations of Critical-Line Reduction for riemannZeta

Notably, the upper layer of the archive contains three distinct proof modules deriving pure RiemannHypothesis from EveryCharacter:

  • Route 1 (Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLine.lean:29-32 → Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/RhOfRight.lean:5-62): The route adopted by rhOfAll in Main.lean:4 and Main.lean:6. rh_of_every (Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLine.lean:29-32) combines h 1 (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ 1) with LFunction_modOne_eq to obtain right half-plane zeta nonvanishing Re(s) > 1/2 ∧ s ≠ 1 ⟹ ζ(s) ≠ 0, passing it to Formalism.VW.rh_of_right (Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/RhOfRight.lean:5-62). Rather than passing through the completed zeta function, rh_of_right applies the uncompleted functional equation riemannZeta_one_sub (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean:178-180) directly at the argument 1 - s (Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/RhOfRight.lean:28-29):

0 = ζ(s) = ζ(1 - (1 - s)) = 2(2π)-(1 - s) Γ(1 - s) cos(π(1 - s)2) ζ(1 - s).

When Re(s) < 1/2, we have Re(1 - s) > 1/2 > 0, whence (i) the exponential prefactor satisfies 2(2π)-(1-s) ≠ 0 (`h2pi`, lines `31-32`), (ii) the Gamma factor satisfies Γ(1 - s) ≠ 0 (`hG`, line `33`), and (iii) the zeta factor satisfies ζ(1 - s) ≠ 0 (`hz'`, line `30`, since ζ(0) = -1/2 ≠ 0 forces s ≠ 0 ⟹ 1 - s ≠ 1). Finally, (iv) assuming cos(π(1-s)/2) = 0 (lines `34-59`) gives 1 - s = 2k + 1 ⟺ s = -2k (k ∈ ℤ): if k < 0, then Re(s) = -2k ≥ 2 > 1/2, a contradiction (lines `45-46`); if k = 0, then s = 0, contradicting ζ(0) = -1/2 ≠ 0 (lines `47-49`); and if k > 0, setting n = k - 1 ∈ ℕ gives s = -2(n + 1), contradicting the trivial-zero exclusion hypothesis `htriv` (lines `50-58`). Because all four factors are nonzero, their product cannot vanish, eliminating the entire open left half-plane Re(s) < 1/2 (including Re(s) ≤ 0) in a single sweep.
  • Route 2 (Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/RiemannHypothesisOfEveryCharacter.lean:211-231): The route invoked by UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.riemannHypothesis in Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/MainConclusion.lean:13-14. Using the completed zeta symmetry completedRiemannZeta_one_sub (Λ(s) = Λ(1-s), line 222) and riemannZeta_def_of_ne_zero (ζ(s) = Λ(s)/Γℝ(s), line 224), it proves in 17 lines that for Re(s) < 1/2, Λ(s) = 0 implies ζ(1-s) = 0 contradicting zeta_ne_zero_of_everyCharacter (lines 211-213), whereas Γℝ(s) = 0 forces s = 0 or s = -2(n+1) via Gammaℝ_eq_zero_iff (line 227).
  • Route 3 (Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/ClaimStrip.lean:75-103): Recorded in claimAll.2.2 : Claim.Zeta, this route handles the open strip 0 < Re(s) < 1 by specializing Claim.strip to N = 1 and closes the exterior regions Re(s) ≥ 1 and Re(s) ≤ 0 via the classical Mathlib theorem riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_le_re (lines 83, 100).

1.3 Core Epistemological Distinction: Type I (Paper-Equivalent Propositions) vs. Type II (Archive-Specific Structure and Sub-Locus Propositions)

Inferring from identifiers alone, such as HarishChandraModules, CasselmanWallach, HasseNormSt, or L2ExtensionLogCanonical, that the underlying def ... : Prop is one-to-one equivalent to the general graduate-textbook theorem leads to serious misinterpretation. In this audit, every mathematical proposition across PublishedTheorems and the 201 direct imports is classified strictly into three categories according to its exact source type signature.

  • Type I (General Propositions Equivalent to Original Papers and Textbooks): Propositions formulated over standard Mathlib categories (NumberField, Scheme.{0}, Representation, IsNonarchimedeanLocalField, Valuation) without domain restriction, faithfully stating the general theorem of the original paper. Examples include Bernstein irreducibility of unitary parabolic products (Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/PublishedTheorems/TwistedTraceFormula/BernsteinUnitaryProductIrreducible.lean:10-16), Jacquet-Shalika isobaric rigidity (Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/PublishedTheorems/GaloisCohomology2/StrongMultiplicityOne.lean:189-203), abelian variety [n]-torsion cardinality n2g (Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/PublishedTheorems/Landherr2/DimEqZero.lean:10-11), the Scholze-Weinstein classification of p-divisible groups (Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/PublishedTheorems/Divisors2/ScholzeWeinsteinB.lean:13-24), and Hironaka principalization (Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/PublishedTheorems/Divisors2/GeometricallyConnectedOfIsIsoRestrict.lean:118-126).

  • Type II-A (Specialized Propositions Projected onto Archive-Specific Data Structures): Propositions stated not over an arbitrary reductive group G or general Shimura variety, but exclusively over custom records engineered within this archive to execute the √X-theta lift and Arakelov volume computations. 1.4 Kernel Truth-Value Invariance vs. Asymmetry of Translation Adapter Lemmas for a Condensed Human Monograph

When Type II-A and Type II-B specializations are identified, the primary mathematical-logical principle to distinguish is the asymmetry between soundness of the mechanized formal proof and black-box citation of the published literature by human mathematicians.

First, Type II specializations introduce zero defect whatsoever into the Lean 4 kernel truth value of Main.lean. Inside the formal system, an intermediate classical proposition Parch is not an externally injected axiom (axiom), but an internal cut formula linking a theorem Tlow : ⊢ Parch proved by downstream modules with an implication Thigh : Parch ⊢ RiemannHypothesis proved by upstream modules. By Modus Ponens,

⊢ Parch Parch ⊢ RiemannHypothesis⊢ RiemannHypothesis

not a single archive-internal definition (D7, GrpData, GoodCusp, UnusedSlot72, etc.) survives in the type of the final theorem Main.riemannHypothesis, which reduces purely to Mathlib's standard _root_.RiemannHypothesis. Even in the extreme case of Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/ThetaCorrespondence/ThetaPairLifts/ThirdPlaceSeries/EveryCharacterOfLiteratureOfVWin.lean:505-506, where the return type UnusedSlot72 of siegel_eisenstein_simple_pole is defined as True and discharged by trivial, the kernel verifies that the upstream consumer every_character_of_theta_integrals_local_matching deduces EveryCharacter without using any information from that slot, preserving the truth value of the final theorem at 100%.

Second, when human mathematicians write a condensed human-readable monograph of roughly 150 pages by citing published papers as black boxes instead of reading 13.15 million lines of internal reproof code, a 'Translation Adapter Lemma' must be established for every Type II proposition. Because a condensed human paper discards the internal proof ⊢ Parch and replaces it with a classical theorem Tlit from the literature, logical completeness requires the bridge implication

Tlit ⟹ Parch

to hold. For Type II-B (sub-locus weakening), the general theorem usually implies the special case immediately (∀ L/F cyclic ⟹ ∀ F(√δ)/F quadratic), making the adapter routine. For Type II-A (custom-structure projection), however, three adapter verifications are indispensable.

Nonlinear / Covering-Group Category Compatibility: Classical theorems on Harish-Chandra modules, Casselman-Wallach globalization, and discrete series are ordinarily stated for connected semisimple matrix Lie groups or reductive groups of Harish-Chandra class (class ℋ). Applying them to GrpData p q requires an adapter lemma verifying that the det 1/2 double cover G = {(g, w) ∈ U(p,q) × ℂ× ∣ w2 = det g} of U(p,q) is a closed matrix Lie subgroup with finite center (a real algebraic subgroup inside GLp+q(ℂ) × GL1(ℂ)) satisfying the Harish-Chandra class axioms.

Measure, Height, and Sign Normalization Consistency: SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent and RallisInnerProductConvergent state identities under the archive's custom Tamagawa and lattice-covolume condition IsCovolOne (ratL B A) μ 𝓨 and sesquilinear conjugation conventions. The mathematical division of labor between the two specifications is as follows.

  1. Weil Absolute-Convergence Range (WeilSiegelFormulaUnitary, rB > 2 rA): Under Weil's convergence criterion indWitt(B) = 0 or rA + indWitt(B) < rB, the theta kernel Θω(g, h; f) is absolutely integrable over [U(B)] = U(B)(F)∖ U(B)(𝔸F) and dominated by a continuous Schwartz seminorm ν(φ) (L59-62). In the strict convergence range rB > 2 rA, the coset series over the Siegel parabolic quotient PSieg(F)∖ U(A ⊕ -A)(F) converges absolutely (CosetConv) and equals the normalized mean theta integral pointwise (Weil 1965):

    ∑γ ∈ PSieg(F)∖ U(A ⊕ (-A))(F) Φf(γ g) = 1vol([U(B)]ν) ∫[U(B)] Θω(g, h; f) dν(h) (rB > 2 rA)

  2. Ichino Half-Convergent / Analytic-Continuation Range (SiegelWeilUnitaryConvergent, rA < rB ≤ 2 rA): In this interval, the Siegel Eisenstein series E(g, s; Φf) fails to converge absolutely at the evaluation point s0 = rB - rA2 (sZero A B), whereas the theta integral still converges absolutely under Weil's inequality rA + indWitt(B) < rB. The source text states that for any archimedean polynomial Fock vector f (IsFockVec) aligned with Cartan involutions (IsCartanInv), the Eisenstein series attached to the flat section flat A a (swSec ... f) s0 admits a holomorphic analytic-continuation value (Eis.EisValueAt) at s = s0 equal to the theta mean thetaMean ω ν f. This is the D7 projection (Type II-A) of the half-convergent Siegel-Weil theorem established beyond Kudla-Rallis (1994) by Ichino (2001, 2004, A regularized Siegel-Weil formula for unitary groups, Math. Z. 247).

Given a projective invariant polyhedral cone decomposition φ : InvFun (𝓞 E) without self-intersection (NoSelfInt, with existence supplied by SiegelToroidalIntegral.exists_fan at L56-61), the signature requires for every level l and moduli space Xo : Moduli Dw l a compactified model Y and effective Cartier boundary divisor BD satisfying five geometric properties (Type II-A): (i) the generic-fiber structure morphism genStr Y is smooth of relative dimension p q (Dw.dim), (ii) the boundary ideal genBdIdeal Y forms a simple-normal-crossings (Snc) divisor, (iii) the boundary support is disjoint from the interior abelian locus abLocus and admits Mumford semi-abelian degenerating complete local charts (HasChartOf φ Y BD d x) near every boundary point x ∈ genBd(Y), (iv) twisting a high tensor power of the Hodge determinant bundle ωY = det Ω1G/Y (detOm Y) down by a positive multiple k · BD of the boundary (polOf Y k BD, a perturbed pullback of the minimal Baily-Borel bundle) yields an ample line bundle (IsAmpleLB), and (v) the algebraic logarithmic Kodaira-Spencer map is an isomorphism on the interior locus (HasLogKS).

Second, governing Arakelov heights and small-section counts on this toroidal model, Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/PublishedTheorems/Divisors2/SmallSecTensTriv.lean:65-97 (in_degree = 257) formalizes for an arithmetically nef (L.IsNef D) Hermitian line bundle L = (L, ‖·‖) on an integral arithmetic variety p : X → Spec 𝒪k of relative dimension D (IsArithVar p D) both finiteness of the set of integral small sections Ĥ0small(X, L⊗ m) := (L.pow m).smallSec (pointwise norm squared at most 1 at all infinite places) and the asymptotic arithmetic Hilbert-Samuel formula (of_triv, L65-69):

log # Ĥ0small(X, L⊗ m) = aΓ(D + 2) mD + 1 + o(mD + 1) (m → ∞)

where a ∈ ℝ is the (D+1)-fold Arakelov self-intersection number (L.IsSelfInter a) of L. At L89-97, theorem volNef divides this asymptotic expansion by mD+1 / Γ(D+2) and takes limsup to deduce that Moriwaki's arithmetic volume vol̂(L) of an arithmetically nef line bundle equals its self-intersection number a (Gillet-Soulé 1992, Zhang 1995, Moriwaki 2000, Yuan 2008). Combined with the Poincaré-Lelong current-based intersection calculus (arCalc_direct, cycleHeights_direct) in Development/WeilBound/CoreStatements/TemperedRepresentationTheory/ArakelovCycleHeights/CycleHeightFormulas/CycleHeightsDirect.lean:138-147 and Yuan's (2008) arithmetic Siu-type volume inequality vol̂(L - M) ≥ (LD+1) - (D+1)(LD · M) (VolGe) in Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/DivisorProofs/VolGeOfHilbertSamuel.lean:26-86, this completes the arithmetic-geometric engine producing nonvanishing algebraic automorphic sections on Shimura varieties.

Volume 3 · Formalism Four Pillars (2.58M Lines) Lower Hubs & Tactics

Volume 3. Deep Decompilation of Lower Tactics and Core Hubs Across the Four Pillars of the New Core Formalism (2,577,937 Lines)

This third volume decompiles into human-readable mathematical equations and theorem chains the lower core hubs and *Proofs/ tactic bodies of the four pillars of Formalism (LocalToGlobal, SharpRestriction, HermitianCurvature, and PeriodIntegrals, totaling 14,866 files, 2,577,937 lines, and 196,578 declarations), which form the central axis of the new mathematical engine in the Riemann Hypothesis formal proof archive by Levent Alpöge and Claude, by opening and inspecting the original Lean source files directly.

Preliminary forensic work verified only the 38 top-level Statement* specification files of Formalism without inspecting the internal implementation of the 2,577,937 lines across the four pillars beneath them. Taking the reference in-degree (in_degree) and shortest import distance (dist) maps extracted in the Part B full AST atlas (B01 to B04) as a compass, this volume reads line by line the most heavily imported algebraic and analytic hub files of each pillar and reconstructs as closed-form mathematical equations the automorphic multiplicity stacking, iterated Parseval Gram matrix upper bounds, Archimedean regularized truncation twin generator, and triple cancellation formulas (Rallis seesaw, Chowla-Selberg, and Siegel mass) operating inside them.

Three architectural characteristics stand out from this quantitative distribution.

  1. Concentration of structure density and algebraic interfaces: Of the 2,018 structure declarations across the four pillars, 1,801 (89.25%) reside in LocalToGlobal (1,151) and SharpRestriction (650). These two pillars serve as the assembly framework for local-to-global compatibility, passing records bundling dozens of arithmetic and automorphic hypothesis fields (LinksStage.Inputs, AllTied, FamP, LocalSituation.Sit, AsmIface.Shd) as parameters.

  2. Sharp contrast in average lines per file: HermitianCurvature averages 239.75 lines per file (460,802 / 1,922) and contains multi-thousand-line continuous analysis and Lie group integration proofs in single files such as Formalism/HermitianCurvature/HermitianCurvatureProofs/UnipotentCoordinatesMeasurePreserving.lean:1-6929. Conversely, PeriodIntegrals is partitioned most finely at 103.87 lines per file (451,856 / 4,350), splitting local volume factor evaluations of the unitary group mass formula into 4,350 atomic modules to eliminate parallel compilation bottlenecks.

  3. Front-line placement at shortest distance dist = 6 to 7 from Main.lean: All four pillars interlock directly with the outer Development.* and CompanionTheory.* welding layers at dist = 6 or dist = 7. Rather than acting as deep foundational utility libraries, the four pillars operate directly one step below the top-level Riemann Hypothesis contradiction argument, delivering the main inequalities of the proof engine.

Differences in tactic ratios across pillars reflect the mathematical objects handled by each pillar.

  • Concentration of omega (4,675 calls) and linarith/nlinarith (3,319 calls) in SharpRestriction: Because Pillar 2 controls the 5-adic level depth j0 = ⌈ log 5(n N(m)/m)⌉+, power truncation exponents of Galois deformation rings, and polyhedral lattice-point count upper bounds, it exhibits the highest frequency among the four pillars of the natural-number division/inequality decision procedure omega and the real linear arithmetic solver linarith.
  • Concentration of simp/simpa (34.21%) and calc (1,539 calls) in HermitianCurvature: Because Pillar 3 expands commutators of Lie differential operator words (Dw) and Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities for sesquilinear forms on the pseudo-unitary group U(p,q), it relies heavily on calc chains and normalizations of the form simp only [Matrix.mul_assoc].
  • Custom tactic kexactB for bypassing elaborator unification delays: Inside LocalToGlobal, where large algebraic records are deeply nested, a dedicated tactic macro is defined in Formalism/LocalToGlobal/IndefiniteReal/HeckeNonvanishing/Imports.lean:1-8 (in_degree = 45, dist = 7) to avoid metavariable unification slowdowns in the default Lean 4 elaborator.
-- Source: Formalism/LocalToGlobal/IndefiniteReal/HeckeNonvanishing/Imports.lean:1-8
import Mathlib
open Lean Elab Tactic Meta in
elab "kexactB " t:term : tactic => withMainContext do
  let goal ← getMainGoal
  let e ← elabTerm t none
  goal.assign e

kexactB elaborates the term t independently first with expectedType set to none, and then assigns it directly to the main goal metavariable via goal.assign e. By bypassing expensive higher-order unification between the expected type and the witness term and letting the kernel type checker verify final type equality directly, it keeps compilation times linear across automorphic package gluing files containing hundreds of fields.

(1) Formalism/Statement.lean:11-50 (50 lines, dist = 9) - Chebyshev-Weighted von Mangoldt Remainder G(x) and Landau Contradiction Specification

The source lines Formalism/Statement.lean:11-23 define the truncated sum S(x) of the von Mangoldt function Λ(n) and its main-term-corrected remainder G(x) as follows:

S(x) := ∑n=1⌊ x ⌋ Λ(n) max(0, xn - 1), γF(x) := x(log x - 1 - γ) + 1, G(x) := S(x) - γF(x)

Next, Formalism/Statement.lean:32-49 declares the Landau positivity contradiction steps LandauStep and LandauStepEps together with the final target proposition RHofG (Formalism/Statement.lean:46-49). RHofG is the one-sided upper bound contradiction principle stating that if G(x) ≤ C xθ + ε holds for all sufficiently large x ≥ x0 for every θ ∈ [1/2, 1) and ε > 0, then ζ(s) ≠ 0 on the half-plane Re(s) > θ. Rather than requiring a two-sided complex modulus bound |G(x)|, a real one-sided upper bound G(x) ≤ C xθ+ε suffices: this asymmetry is the starting point across all four pillars for deducing zero-freeness from the positivity of Hermitian Gram matrices (0 ≤ ⟨ Θ f, Θ f ⟩).

(2) Formalism/StatementOC.lean:11-73 (73 lines, dist = 8) - Dirichlet Character Combined Remainder Gχ(x) and Weighted Average OCAvg

Formalism/StatementOC.lean:11-22 imports Formalism.Statement and declares the twisted sum Sχ(x) and main-term-corrected remainder Gχ(x) for a Dirichlet character χ modulo q:

Sχ(x) := ∑n=1⌊ x ⌋ Λ(n)χ(n)max(0, xn - 1), Gχ(x) := Sχ(x) + L'(1, χ)L(1, χ) x

It then defines OCStep (Formalism/StatementOC.lean:23-30), the Chebyshev-weighted average version OCAvgUpper (Formalism/StatementOC.lean:52-64), and RiemannHypothesisOfLowerBounds (Formalism/StatementOC.lean:65-72). Inside Pillar 2 SharpRestriction, the key output hub Formalism/SharpRestriction/RamificationFrobenius/TotientGaloisClasses/ExplicitFormulaErrorOfHostConditions.lean:2 (168 lines, dist = 7, in_degree = 10) imports Formalism.StatementOC directly and constructs the combined linear form Λ.Gm(y) (Formalism/SharpRestriction/RamificationFrobenius/TotientGaloisClasses/ExplicitFormulaErrorOfHostConditions.lean:38) over a finite primitive-character level Λ : Level:

Λ.Gm(y) := Gz(y) + ∑ψ ∈ Λ.Nt Λ.wt(ψ) Re(gχ(ψ.χ, y)), Λ.wt(ψ) := 1 (Λ.psK = some ψ)
(3 Λ.o + 1)-1 (otherwise)

Here the weight (3 Λ.o + 1)-1 (Formalism/SharpRestriction/RamificationFrobenius/TotientGaloisClasses/ExplicitFormulaErrorOfHostConditions.lean:36) is the decisive coefficient enforcing positivity of coset indicator functions over a character subgroup of order Λ.o = |Ξ|, and theorem EAtH.explicit_formula_error_of_host_conditions (Formalism/SharpRestriction/RamificationFrobenius/TotientGaloisClasses/ExplicitFormulaErrorOfHostConditions.lean:155-165) in the same file derives the explicit-formula error package EAtH from HostConditions.

(3) Formalism/StatementU.lean:9-47 (47 lines, dist = 10) - Chebyshev Window Average wavg and Mellin-Landau Analytic Continuation

Formalism/StatementU.lean:9-13 defines the normalized remainder Gz(x) := Gz(x) + x - 1 and the discrete window average wavg m x f of length m:

wavg(m, x, f) := 1m∑j=1m f((1 + j2m) x)

The proposition ZetaLandauBarEps (Formalism/StatementU.lean:29-33) specifies that ζ(s) ≠ 0 for Re(s) > θ follows from the window-average upper bound wavg(m, x, Gz) ≤ C xθ + ε with m ≥ x1 - θ - ε. This specification is realized in Formalism/ZetaNonvanishing/ZetaLandau.lean:18-99 (300 lines, dist = 11) via the Mellin transform identity mellin_HZ (Formalism/ZetaNonvanishing/ZetaLandau.lean:75-91). Specifically, for HZ(ε, C, θ; x) := ε Gz(x) + C xθ ≥ 0, its Mellin integral IZ(s) = ∫1∞ HZ(x) x-s-1 dx is proved on Re(s) > 1 to equal

ΦZ(ε, C, θ; s) = ε nZ(s)s(s - 1) + Cs - θ, nZ(s) := -ζ1'(s)ζ1(s) - 1 + (1 + γ)s

(PhiZ_eq, Formalism/ZetaNonvanishing/ZetaLandau.lean:93-98), blocking both real and complex zeros via Landau's real-axis singularity theorem for non-negative integrands.

(4) Formalism/StatementCM.lean:9-45 (45 lines, dist = 13) and Formalism/StatementFL.lean:11-44 (44 lines, dist = 15) - CM Half-Type Partition and Odd-Character Killing Formula

2.3 Core Mathematical Reconstruction: +1 Automorphic Multiplicity Stacking Along Totally Definite Unitary Chains U(X0) → … → U(Xm) (m ≈ √x) and Derivative-Free Stepanov Evaluation

In classical proofs of the function-field Riemann Hypothesis (the Stepanov-Bombieri method), one constructs an auxiliary polynomial Φ on a curve 𝒞/𝔽q over a finite field and applies Hasse-Schmidt hyperderivatives D(r)Φ to force high vanishing multiplicity m at Frobenius fixed points. Over ℚ and ℤ, however, no global derivation preserving the Leibniz rule across all primes exists. The core mechanism implemented in LocalToGlobal replaces differential vanishing-order elevation with m-fold composition of primitive theta links (PrimitiveLinks) along a totally definite unitary group chain of length m ≈ √x, multiplicatively stacking automorphic spectral multiplicities and Arakelov normalization factors by +1 per step. The exact parameter scales and operator equations reconstructed from the source code proceed in four steps.

Step 1: Source Fixation of the Parameter Scale Window (m, n, k) (Formalism/SharpRestriction/InertJacobiLevels/AsmIface.lean:142-144)

Given an asymptotic scale x → ∞ and a small exponent ε ∈ (0, 1/52) (Formalism/SharpRestriction/ParConsts.lean:99-100), the lift-chain length m := D.R.m, evaluation-dimension parameter n := D.R.n, and base unitary rank k := D.R.k are strictly pinned by Formalism/SharpRestriction/InertJacobiLevels/AsmIface.lean:142-144 to the intervals

√x δ1 ≤ m ≤ 2√x δ1, x2 + 8ε ≤ n ≤ 2 x2 + 8ε, x92 + 10ε ≤ k ≤ 2 x92 + 10ε

Here δ1 > 0 is a fixed density constant, so the chain length m has exact order Θ(√x).

Step 2: Unitary Hermitian Chain and Stepwise Rallis Scalar Action (Formalism/LocalToGlobal/IndefiniteReal/BaseLiftsPackageOfPrimitiveLinks.lean:68-73)

For a fixed odd rank stride t := P.t, consider a sequence of totally definite Hermitian spaces over a totally real field F,

X0 ⟶ X1 ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ Xj ⟶ Xj+1 ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ Xm

(Formalism/SharpRestriction/Divisibility/FunctionModelRallisFromInputs.lean:577-581, rkE(Xj+1) = rkE(Xj) + (t + 1), Witt index wittIdx(Xj) = 0) paired with the companion indefinite sequence Yc D i (Formalism/LocalToGlobal/IndefiniteReal/LinksStage.lean:240). At each link j ∈ {0, …, m-1}, the Weil representation on the adelic unitary product U(Xj)(𝔸F) × U(Xj+1)(𝔸F) together with a test vector Φj ∈ 𝒮(Xj ⊗ Xj+1)(𝔸F) (Formalism/LocalToGlobal/IndefiniteReal/DatumVec.lean:84-105) defines the integral theta lift operator

θj, t : 𝒜cusp(U(Xj)) ⟶ 𝒜cusp(U(Xj+1)), (θj,t f)(h) := ∫[U(Xj)] ΘΦj, μj+1(g, h) f(g) dg

(by total definiteness wittIdx(Xj) = 0, every automorphic form automatically belongs to the cuspidal space X.cusp V = ⊤ under ThetaCuspidalityCondition at Formalism/SharpRestriction/Divisibility/FunctionModelRallisFromInputs.lean:527-528). Proposition PThmA at Formalism/LocalToGlobal/IndefiniteReal/BaseLiftsPackageOfPrimitiveLinks.lean:68-70 states that at each step j, the adjoint composition θj,t ∘ θj,t* acts as a positive scalar multiple on the designated local-global Hecke and K-type eigenspace Wj, p, v0:

.(θj, t ∘ θj, t*)‖Wj, p, v0 = λj, t, p, v0 · idWj, p, v0, λj, t, p, v0 > 0

Step 3: Eigenvalue Stacking of the m-Fold Composite Gram Operator (thmBop_of and DetChain)

Starting from the 0-th base space, form the global lift operator Θt := θm-1, t ∘ ⋯ ∘ θ1, t ∘ θ0, t by composing m consecutive primitive links. PThmB at Formalism/LocalToGlobal/IndefiniteReal/BaseLiftsPackageOfPrimitiveLinks.lean:71-73, theorem prod_lamN (:110-125), and thmBop_of (:184-196) recursively combine the stepwise scaled-isometry hypotheses with the phase-cancellation lemma phase_cancel (:130-161) to prove that on every element e of the terminal subspace Ep, v0, the composite Gram operator Θt ∘ Θt* acts by the exact product of the m stepwise eigenvalues:

(Θt ∘ Θt*)(e) = (κ ∏j=0m-1 λj, t, p, v0) e

Moreover, in the general family setting where each step acts as a multi-row block operator Bj ∈ Endℂ(E) rather than a scalar, proposition DetChain in Formalism/ThetaLiftIndependence/Statement.lean:266-277 (301 lines, in_degree = 19, dist = 9) establishes that the determinant of the composite Gram matrix A := Θt ∘ Θt* factors as

det (A) = κdim ℂ E ∏j=0m-1 det (Bj)

Each traversal of a link U(Xj) → U(Xj+1) stacks one additional factor λj, t, p, v0 arising from central L-values and local volume ratios onto the exponent, building a multiplicative amplification ∏j=0m-1 λj ≍ Λgainm across m steps.

Step 4: Coupling with Derivative-Free Shortened Evaluation ShortValAt (Formalism/LocalToGlobal/ProjectiveLattices/ThShort.lean:244-262)

Finally, when evaluating the terminal automorphic form Θt(f0) on U(Xm) along special CM cycles, ShortValAt at Formalism/LocalToGlobal/ProjectiveLattices/ThShort.lean:244-262 multiplies a weight-a harmonic polynomial P ∈ harmL(Λ, a) on the abelian scheme by the level normalization factor (N : c.F)-deg P to extract the algebraic value

ShortValAt(∇, w, Λ, β; P) := N-deg P evx0(β-a DP(sw)) ∈ 𝒪K0[1bad]

Here P(∇) acts solely on the geometric Gauss-Manin / Maass-Shimura differential sheaf of bounded finite degree and takes no high-order derivatives in the rational prime p direction. Instead, the Θ(√x)-order multiplicity needed to dominate the number of prime evaluation points is supplied entirely by the eigenvalue product ∏j=0m-1 λj of the m-step unitary theta chain together with the Arakelov line-bundle degree lower bound. This is the exact Lean 4 realization of derivative-free automorphic Stepanov multiplicity over ℤ.

3.3 Core Mathematical Reconstruction: Iterated Parseval Identity and the GL5 6-Fold Metaplectic Cover Relative Trace / Schur Upper-Bound Chain

In analytic number theory, bounding inner-product matrices ⟨ Pu, Pu' ⟩ of Poincaré series via classical Kuznetsov-Petersson trace formulas relies on pointwise phase cancellation in individual Kloosterman or Gauss sums (such as the Weil bound q1/2). At multiply ramified levels on higher-rank unitary and general linear groups (GL5 and above), however, degenerate hyperboloid singularities in high-dimensional exponential sums prevent pointwise phase cancellation alone from avoiding exponent loss.

The solution built in SharpRestriction dispenses with sign cancellation in individual Gauss sums altogether, combining iterated Parseval identities over quotient-module cokernels, a relative trace formula on the 6-fold metaplectic cover of GL5, and a C*-algebraic functional-calculus Schur lemma to compress Hilbert-Schmidt and operator norms of Gram matrices into purely non-negative L2 sums of squares. The exact four-step equation chain recorded in the source code runs as follows.

Step 1: Iterated Parseval Identity Over Cokernel Isomorphism Classes (Kk_succ) Replacing Gauss-Sum Cancellation

Formalism/SharpRestriction/CuspSpanNormBounds/FractionFieldToGenericStalkAlgebraMapEq.lean:42-260 defines over a non-Archimedean local field extension E/F the split model Model F E (:42-47), subring of integers R := M.R ⊆ E (:52-60), additive character ψR : E → ℂ× (:66-70), cokernels M.Cok ZZ (:90-92) of size-(m+1) matrices, and the set of isomorphism classes Clsm(M) := M.Cls m (:143, with automorphism-group order |Aut(c)| = M.nAut c at :145).

Defining the partial Bessel integral coefficients BB(M; w, c) ∈ ℂ (:211-214) with respect to lower- and upper-triangular unipotent matrices uLow(x) (:181-183) and uUp(w, y) (:184-187), theorem Kk_succ (Formalism/SharpRestriction/CuspSpanNormBounds/FractionFieldToGenericStalkAlgebraMapEq.lean:254-256) proves that the kernel Kk := M.Kk (:215-218) ascending from depth m to depth m+1 satisfies the exact Parseval decomposition identity

Km+1(w, w') = ∑c ∈ Clsm(M) BB(M; w, c) BB(M; w', c)|Aut(c)|

In particular, along the diagonal w = w',

Km+1(w, w) = ∑c ∈ Clsm(M) ‖BB(M; w, c)‖2|Aut(c)| ≥ 0

so L2 mass is preserved identically across dimensions 1 → 2 → … → rS + 1 by orthogonality (Parseval's identity) over the finite abelian cokernel M.Cok ZZ, without estimating pointwise cancellation of complex oscillatory terms. Off the diagonal (w ≠ w'), Cauchy-Schwarz yields |Km+1(w, w')|2 ≤ Km+1(w, w) Km+1(w', w') immediately.

    • If the real spectrum spectrum ℝ T contained two distinct points a < b, one constructs two non-negative continuous cutoff functions f1, f2 : ℝ → ℝ with disjoint supports (f1(a) > 0, f2(b) > 0, f1 · f2 = 0).

    • Hence the spectrum collapses to a singleton {c}, and cfc_id yields T = c · idH.

5.3 The σ = 23 Level-Denominator Loss Barrier in Iterated Lifts: Source Reconstruction of Arakelov Projective-Lattice Degree Descent

Opening the source equations of Formalism/PeriodIntegrals/DivisionRowsRationalLattice.lean:62-251 (283 lines, in_degree = 32) reveals with complete mathematical clarity why naive iterated theta lifts or classical auxiliary-polynomial constructions hit a zero-free barrier at σ = 23, and how the archive breaks past it.

(1) Denominator-n Loss Formula at a Single Projection Step (DegreeKernelLowerBound)

Consider an Arakelov Hermitian lattice A : HLat K over a number field K (with underlying 𝒪K-lattice L := A.L, maximal slope μmax(L) := muMaxL A L, and Arakelov degree deg (L) := degL A L) together with a self-adjoint idempotent projection e ∈ EndK(A.V) (e2 = e). When e fails to preserve the integral lattice L on the nose and satisfies only n · e(L) ⊆ L for a positive integer denominator n ∈ ℕ>0 (IsProj A e n, Formalism/PeriodIntegrals/DivisionRowsRationalLattice.lean:62-65), a finite torsion quotient arises between the kernel-cut lattice cute(L) := L ∩ ker (1 - e) and the projected image lattice imge(L) := e(L). ProjectionSandwichLength (:74-86) and GramDetKernelValuation (:192-196) bound the index loss and Gram-determinant valuation growth at each finite place w by

idxw(imge(L), cute(L)) ≤ min(dim e, dim (1 - e)) vw(n), vw(det h|cute(L)) ≤ 2 dim (1 - e) vw(n)

Summing across all places, DegreeKernelLowerBound (Formalism/PeriodIntegrals/DivisionRowsRationalLattice.lean:87-89) records the Arakelov degree lower bound after a single projection:

deg (cute(L)) ≥ deg (L) - dim K(1 - e) · (μmax(L) + 2log n)

(2) Origin of the σ = 23 Barrier Under Naive m-Fold Sequential Projections

Suppose that along an m-step lift chain U(X0) → U(X1) → … → U(Xm), one applied Hecke/parahoric projections ej sequentially at each step j = 1, …, m, allowing both the denominator penalty 2log nj and the maximal-slope increment Δ μmax to accumulate step by step. Because at step j the maximal slope μmax(Lj) would itself have grown by the prior denominator losses ∑i < j O(log x), the cumulative Arakelov height loss (finite-place denominator inflation) across all m steps would incur a quadratic cost Ω(m2 · rk · log x) (or level-product blowup Ω(m3 log x)). Meanwhile, the main-term cancellation gain from m-step multiplicity stacking over a window of width x / m scales linearly in m. Balancing the analytic window remainder x · m-1 against a quadratic denominator cost m2 yields

xm ≍ m2 ⟺ m ≍ x13 ⟹ error exponent x1 - 13 = x23 (σ = 23)

trapping the exponent at 23 and preventing m from ever reaching √x.

    [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [Module (𝓞 K) V] [IsScalarTower (𝓞 K) K V] [Fintype ι]

    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] (b : Basis ι K V) (X : InfinitePlace K → Matrix ι ι ℂ)

def dimFl (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] (N : ℕ) : ℕ := Fintype.card ι * (N * (N - 1) / 2)

def permExp {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] {N : ℕ} (σ : ι → Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) : (ι × Fin N) →0 ℕ :=

def degFl (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (N : ℕ) (P : MvPolynomial (ι × Fin N) ℝ) : ℝ :=

4.1 Generalized Progression-Free Behrend Sets and Cyclic-Group Orbit Windows (BehrendSets)

In Formalism.BehrendSets (14 files, 1,074 lines), Formalism/BehrendSets/Statement.lean:48 specifies verbatim BehrendFree (extending classical three-term progression avoidance x1 - 2x2 + x3 = 0 to arbitrary integer coefficient height K ≥ 1), the subexponential density lower bound BehrendBound, and the thick-translate window intersection theorems WindowTwo and OrbitOne over the cyclic group ℤ/nℤ:

def BehrendFree (K : ℕ) (T : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ α β γ : ℤ, α ≠ 0 → β ≠ 0 → γ ≠ 0 → α + β + γ = 0 →
    |α| ≤ (K : ℤ) → |β| ≤ (K : ℤ) → |γ| ≤ (K : ℤ) →
    ∀ x1 ∈ T, ∀ x2 ∈ T, ∀ x3 ∈ T,
      α * (x1 : ℤ) + β * (x2 : ℤ) + γ * (x3 : ℤ) = 0 → x1 = x2 ∧ x2 = x3

def BehrendBound : Prop := ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ K N : ℕ, 1 ≤ K → 1 ≤ N →
  ∃ T : Finset ℕ, T ⊆ range N ∧ BehrendFree K T ∧
    (N : ℝ) * Real.exp (-C * Real.sqrt (Real.log N * Real.log ((K : ℝ) + 1))) ≤ (T.card : ℝ)

def ThickSet : Prop := ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n L : ℕ, 1 ≤ L → 8 * L ≤ n →
  ∃ T : Finset ℕ, (∀ t ∈ T, 8 * L * t < n) ∧ BehrendFree (2 * L) T ∧
    (n : ℝ) / (8 * L) * Real.exp (-C * Real.sqrt (Real.log n * Real.log (2 * (L : ℝ) + 1)))
      ≤ (T.card : ℝ)

def thick (n : ℕ) (T : Finset ℕ) (u : ZMod n) : Finset (ZMod n) :=
  T.image (fun t : ℕ => ((t : ℕ) : ZMod n) + u)

def WindowTwo : Prop := ∀ (n L : ℕ) [NeZero n] (T : Finset ℕ),
  (∀ t ∈ T, 8 * L * t < n) → BehrendFree (2 * L) T →
  ∀ h u t0 : ZMod n, 2 * L < addOrderOf h → ∀ j : ℤ,
    ((Finset.Ico j (j + 2 * (L : ℤ))).filter (fun i : ℤ => t0 + i • h ∈ thick n T u)).card ≤ 2

The mathematical mechanism interlocking these four statements reconstructs in three steps.

First, Behrend spherical-shell density lower bound (BehrendBound, :54): For fixed coefficient bound K, there exists a subset T ⊆ {0, …, N-1} admitting no nontrivial solution to α x1 + β x2 + γ x3 = 0 (α + β + γ = 0, 0 < |α|, |β|, |γ| ≤ K) while achieving cardinality

|T| ≥ N exp(-C √log N · log (K + 1))

Expanding integers in base B ≈ exp(√log N / log (K+1)) into high-dimensional lattice digits (d0, …, dm-1) ∈ {0, …, ⌊ B/(2K) ⌋ - 1}m eliminates base-B carries altogether, and strict convexity on a spherical shell ∑r dr2 = R collapses any three linearly dependent points to a single point, yielding the stated density lower bound by the pigeonhole principle.

Second, elimination of modulo-n wrap-around and at-most-two-point window intersection (Formalism/BehrendSets/BehrendVariance/SpaceFreeOfBehrendFree.lean:24): Why forming the thick set thick(n, T, u) = (T + u) mod n inside ℤ/nℤ requires both BehrendFree (2 * L) T of coefficient height 2L and the magnitude cap 8Lt < n (∀ t ∈ T) is explained directly by lemma core in Formalism/BehrendSets/BehrendVariance/SpaceFreeOfBehrendFree.lean:24. Suppose three indices i1 < i2 < i3 (i3 - i1 ≤ Lw) inside a window of length Lw = 2L along an element h ∈ ℤ/nℤ of additive order ord+(h) > Lw collide via t0 + ir h ≡ yr + u (mod n) (yr ∈ T). Eliminating t0, u, h by linear combination produces the integer determinant (:32)

D := (i3 - i1)(y2 - y1) - (i2 - i1)(y3 - y1) ∈ ℤ

satisfying D ≡ 0 (mod n), hence n ∣ D (:42). On the other hand, since every y ∈ T satisfies 4 Lw y < n, the triangle inequality gives (:54 to :65)

|D| ≤ |i3 - i1|· |y2 - y1| + |i2 - i1|· |y3 - y1| < Lw · n4 Lw + Lw · n4 Lw = n2 < n

By Int.eq_zero_of_abs_lt_dvd (:66), the congruence modulo n upgrades to the exact integer identity D = 0, which becomes a nontrivial three-term relation α y1 + β y2 + γ y3 = 0 with α = -(i3 - i2), β = i3 - i1, γ = -(i2 - i1) (α + β + γ = 0, |α|, |β|, |γ| ≤ Lw), contradicting BehrendFree (False, :80). Consequently, every window of length 2L meets thick(n, T, u) in at most 2 points (WindowTwo, Formalism/BehrendSets/Statement.lean:67), whereas short-period elements with ord+(h) ≤ 8L meet it in at most 1 point across their entire orbit because 8Lt < n (OrbitOne, :72).

def JacquetSubsetSum : Prop :=
  ∀ (k : Type) [Field k] (r s : ℕ) (b : Fin r → Fin s), Monotone b →
    ∀ (Y : Type) [AddCommGroup Y] [Module ℂ Y] (ρ : GL (Fin r) k → Y →ₗ[ℂ] Y),
    (∀ S : Finset (Fin r), (∃ i j, b i = b j ∧ i ∈ S ∧ j ∉ S) →
      ∀ y : Y, (∀ u : GL (Fin r) k,
        (∀ i j, (u : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) k) i j ≠ (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) k) i j →
          b i = b j ∧ i ∈ S ∧ j ∉ S) → ρ u y = y) → y = 0) →
    ∀ (a : ℕ), a ≤ r → ∀ (φ : GL (Fin r) k → Y),
    (∀ q x : GL (Fin r) k, (∀ i j, b j < b i → (q : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) k) i j = 0) →
      φ (q * x) = ρ q (φ x)) →
    (∀ x n : GL (Fin r) k,
      (∀ i j, (n : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) k) i j ≠ (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) k) i j →
        (i : ℕ) < a ∧ a ≤ (j : ℕ)) → φ (x * n) = φ x) →
    φ ≠ 0 → ∃ J : Finset (Fin s), a = ∑ c ∈ J, (Finset.univ.filter fun i => b i = c).card

def IwahoriNewton : Prop :=
  ∀ (O : Type) [CommRing O] [IsLocalRing O] (ϖ : O), ϖ ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal O →
    ∀ (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → ℕ), StrictAnti a →
    ∀ i1 i2 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) O,
    (∀ i, IsUnit (i1 i i)) → (∀ i, IsUnit (i2 i i)) →
    (∀ i j, j < i → ϖ ∣ i1 i j) → (∀ i j, j < i → ϖ ∣ i2 i j) →
    ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ r → ∃ u : Oˣ,
      (i1 * Matrix.diagonal (fun i => ϖ ^ a i) * i2).charpoly.coeff (r - k) =
        (u : O) * ϖ ^ (∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun j : Fin r => r - k ≤ (j : ℕ)), a j)

Whenever a nonzero induced section φ ≠ 0 satisfying the cuspidal block hypothesis is right-invariant under the upper-triangular unipotent radical of step sizes (a, r - a), the integer a is forced to be a subset sum a = ∑c ∈ J |b-1(c)| of the block sizes; designing the block partition {|b-1(c)|} to avoid unwanted subset sums (GoodImpliesH, :15) therefore annihilates boundary Jacquet components algebraically. Simultaneously, the degree-(r-k) coefficient of the characteristic polynomial of an Iwahori double-coset element i1 · diag(ϖa0, …, ϖar-1) · i2 (a0 > … > ar-1) equals a unit u ∈ 𝒪× times ϖ∑j=r-kr-1 aj, pinning down every vertex of its Newton polygon without error.

def LandauLocal : Prop :=

5.3 Converting an Off-Line Zero Hypothesis ρ0 = β0 + iγ0 into Logarithmic-Derivative Residues and Chebyshev Weighted Positivity (ZetaNonvanishing*)

We now reconstruct directly from the Lean source the analytic engine at the top of the archive that refutes off-line zeros across ZetaRealNonvanish.lean (80 lines), ZetaNonvanishing/ZetaLandau.lean (300 lines), ZetaNonvanishingChebyshevWeights.lean (36 lines), and ZetaNonvanishingGeneralWeights.lean (26 lines).

Step 1: Nonvanishing on the real interval (0, 1) and the differential-equation zero-free criterion (Formalism/ZetaRealNonvanish.lean:63 and :76). First, the archive establishes ζ(σ) ≠ 0 along the real segment σ ∈ (0, 1) (ZetaRealNonvanish, :63) together with real-axis nonvanishing for quadratic characters of conductors 4, 3, 7 (LRealNonvanish, :69). Next, it prepares LogDerivZeroFree (:76): if an entire function P ≢ 0 satisfies P'(s) = q(s) P(s) on an open set U ⊂ ℂ for a function q : U → ℂ holomorphic on U, then P cannot vanish anywhere in U. Indeed, if P(ρ0) = 0 at some ρ0 ∈ U with multiplicity m ≥ 1, then P'(s)P(s) has a simple pole at s = ρ0 of residue m ≠ 0, which cannot equal q(s) holomorphic on U.

Step 2: Mellin transform of the smoothed von Mangoldt remainder Gζ(x) and Landau's theorem (Formalism/ZetaNonvanishing/ZetaLandau.lean:18 to :299). Subtracting the principal part of the double pole at s = 1 from the second Riesz mean Sζ(x) = ∑1 ≤ n ≤ ⌊ x ⌋ Λ(n)(x/n - 1) defines the remainder function

Gζ(x) = Sζ(x) - x log x + (1 + γ) x

(Formalism/StatementOC.lean:13) alongside the regularized entire zeta function ζ1(s) = (s - 1)ζ(s) (riemannZeta1, satisfying ζ1(1) = 1). Introducing the linear correction linZ(s) = -1 + (1 + γ)s (Formalism/ZetaNonvanishing/ZetaLandau.lean:18), AZ(s) = -ζ'1(s) + linZ(s)ζ1(s) (:22, with AZ(1) = 0 at :35), and nZ(s) = -ζ'1(s)ζ1(s) + linZ(s) (:20) gives the Mellin transform identity on Re(s) > 1 (mellin_Gz_n, :46):

∫1∞ Gζ(x) x-s - 1 dx = nZ(s)s(s - 1) = AZ(s) / (s - 1)s ζ1(s)

Suppose now that for some sign s0 ∈ {+1, -1} and exponent θ ∈ (0, 1), a one-sided bound s0 Gζ(x) ≤ C xθ holds for all x ≥ x0. Combining C with a uniform bound B on the compact interval [1, max(x0, 1)] (Gz_bdd, :237) and setting M = max(C, B) and ε0 = -s0 ∈ {+1, -1} (ε02 = 1), the auxiliary integrand (:24 and :266)

HZ(ε0, M, θ; x) := ε0 Gζ(x) + M xθ ≥ 0 (∀ x ≥ 1)

is nonnegative throughout [1, ∞). On Re(s) > 1, its Mellin integral IZ(s) = ∫1∞ HZ(x) x-s-1 dx coincides with the meromorphic function

ΦZ(s) = ε0 dslope(AZ, 1)(s)s ζ1(s) + Ms - θ

(PhiZ_eq_IZ, :100). Because real-axis nonvanishing ZetaRealNonvanish from Step 1 guarantees ζ1(σ) ≠ 0 for every real σ ∈ (θ, 1], the function ΦZ(s) is real-analytic along the entire segment (θ, 1] (PhiZ_analyticAt, :105). Applying Landau's theorem for nonnegative Dirichlet-Mellin kernels (landau_Z, :126), the Mellin integral IZ(s) continues past the abscissa barrier s = 1 to converge absolutely and define a holomorphic function throughout the open half-plane U = {s ∈ ℂ : Re(s) > θ} (:152). By the identity theorem for analytic continuation (AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq, :173), every s ∈ U satisfies

s(s - 1) ζ1(s)(IZ(s) - Ms - θ) = ε0 AZ(s) = ε0(-ζ'1(s) + linZ(s)ζ1(s))

and multiplying by ε02 = 1 yields, for the function q(s) = linZ(s) - ε0 s(s-1)(IZ(s) - Ms-θ) holomorphic on U = {Re(s) > θ} (:188), the differential equation

ζ'1(s) = q(s) ζ1(s) (∀ s ∈ U)

(:197 to :204). Any hypothetical zero ρ0 with β0 = Re(ρ0) > θ would produce a simple-pole residue in ζ'1ζ1 violating this identity; hence LogDerivZeroFree (:206) establishes ζ(s) ≠ 0 for all Re(s) > θ (zetaLandau, :258, together with its ε-slack version zetaLandauEps, :292).

Step 3: Chebyshev node-weighted averages and the Guinand-Weil continuous transform (Formalism/ZetaNonvanishingChebyshevWeights.lean:1 to :36). Geometric trace formulas do not output point values Gζ(x) directly, but rather node-weighted averages wavg. Lines 9 to 35 of Formalism/ZetaNonvanishingChebyshevWeights.lean:9 bridge discrete Chebyshev node averages and continuous integral transforms as follows:

def chebNode (m : ℕ) (j : Fin m) : ℝ := Real.sin ((2 * ((j : ℕ) + 1 : ℝ) - 1) * π / (4 * m)) ^ 2

def chebyshevWeightedAverage (m : ℕ) (x : ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  wavg (fun j : Fin m => x / chebNode m j) (fun _ => (1 : ℝ) / m) x f

def Gcheb (x : ℝ) : ℝ := (1 / π) * ∫ φ in (0 : ℝ)..π, Real.sin (φ / 2) ^ 2 * Gz (x / Real.sin (φ / 2) ^ 2)

def ZetaLandauCheb : Prop :=
  ∀ s0 : ℝ, (s0 = 1 ∨ s0 = -1) → ∀ θ : ℝ, 0 < θ → θ < 1 →
  (∃ C x0 : ℝ, ∀ x : ℝ, x0 ≤ x → s0 * Gcheb x ≤ C * x ^ θ) →
  ∀ s : ℂ, θ < s.re → riemannZeta s ≠ 0

  ∀ s : ℂ, θ < s.re → riemannZeta s ≠ 0

def ChebyshevWeightApproximation : Prop :=
  ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ (m : ℕ) (x : ℝ), 0 < m → 1 ≤ x →
    |chebyshevWeightedAverage m x Gz - Gcheb x| ≤ K * x * (1 + Real.log m) / m

def ZetaNonvanishingChebyshevWeights : Prop :=

Substituting the Chebyshev nodes uj = sin2((2j+1)π4m), sample points xs,j = x / uj, and uniform weights ωj = 1/m into wavg(xs, ω, x, f) = ∑j ωj xxs,j f(xs,j) (Formalism/StatementU.lean:11) yields
